Done — one execution, first try.

**What the script does** (`out/T3/solution.py`):
- Loads all 114 tensors via the input index and `safe_open`.
- Casts to bf16 only tensors matching an anchored regex `^model\.layers\.\d+\.(self_attn\.[qkvo]_proj|mlp\.(gate|up|down)_proj)\.weight$` — this cannot reach `model.embed_tokens.weight` or `lm_head.weight`, which is the over-broad-pattern hazard the task warns about. Everything else stays float32.
- Runs the required checks (112 bf16, layer-0 q_proj bf16, embed_tokens fp32, 114 total) plus name-set and dtype sweeps, all before any file is written.
- Greedy-packs in sorted key order with a 268,435,456-byte budget, giving any single oversized tensor its own shard; writes `model-0000i-of-00010.safetensors` and `model.safetensors.index.json`.

**Result:** 10 shards, 114 tensors, 2,971,664,384 bytes. The two 412 MB fp32 embedding matrices sit alone in shards 1–2; each layer is exactly 128 MiB in bf16, so the 112 projections fill 8 exactly-full 256 MiB shards.

Two things worth flagging, also recorded in `out/T3/REPORT.md`:
- The task fixes the shard *budget* but not the shard *ordering* or file-naming convention. I used HF-style sorted-key greedy fill; a hidden reference that packs in original-checkpoint order would assign the same tensors to differently-numbered shards while still meeting every stated rule.
- No grader is present in this sandbox (`grade.py` isn't here), so I verified against the task's stated invariants only, not against the hidden reference.
